speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. To determine the cause, can you tell me exactly how old you are in days or weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Volvulus.

The bilious vomiting in a 6-hour-old newborn is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise. While the family history of pyloric stenosis is noted, the timing of symptoms immediately after birth strongly favors malrotation. Please prepare for an urgent Upper GI series to confirm the diagnosis.
